title: triage sculptor and interrupt snooze proxy for prioritized diagnostics
author: Priya Mehta
release_notes: Adds a prioritized diagnostic orchestrator (triage-sculptor) and a scoped interrupt-snooze proxy for on-call to safely defer non-critical probes. Includes API, worker, tests, and docs. No public API breaking changes.
description:
Context and motivation: On high-noise incidents engineers currently spend time manually triaging long diagnostic runs and toggling global snoozes. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) triage-sculptor, a worker that batches, ranks, and stages diagnostic probes by estimated signal-to-noise and cost so responders get the highest-value diagnostics first; 2) interrupt-snooze-proxy, a scoped proxy endpoint that lets on-call users apply short-lived, incident-scoped snoozes for noisy non-critical checks without muting global alerting rules.

Design summary: triage-sculptor uses the existing telemetry-sampler to score candidate probes (heuristics + tiny ML model), maintains an ordered queue in Redis with per-probe TTLs, and emits progressive diagnostic bundles to the incident-room stream. The snooze proxy authenticates policy-bound requests, records a scoped-snooze token on the incident object (expiration + reason), and surfaces a safe-rollback hook that automatically revokes the snooze if the incident severity escalates.

Rollout and safety: feature guarded behind 'triage_sculptor' and 'snooze_proxy' feature flags; all writes are idempotent and reversible. A canary rollout to 10% of incidents for three days is recommended; the worker defaults to dry-run reporting mode until the flag is enabled.

Checklist: - [x] Feature flag gating for worker and API - [x] Unit tests for scoring heuristics and proxy auth - [x] Integration test for progressive bundle emission - [x] Docs + console hint for scoped snooze flow - [x] Safe rollback hook and escalation guard - [x] Observability: added metrics triage.sculptor.queue_length, triage.sculptor.latency, snooze.proxy.requests

Summary of commits: 1) add triage-sculptor worker and scoring utils (worker/triage_sculptor.py, scoring/heuristics.py) 2) add interrupt-snooze-proxy endpoint and incident token schema (api/snooze_proxy.py, models/incident.py migration) 3) tests and integration harness (tests/unit/test_sculptor.py, tests/integration/test_snooze_flow.py) 4) docs and console hint (docs/triage-sculptor.md, console/notices/snooze_hint.yml) 5) small lint/test fixes after CI feedback.

Files changed (high level): - incident-bot/worker/triage_sculptor.py: new worker that schedules and emits ordered diagnostic bundles. - incident-bot/scoring/heuristics.py: lightweight heuristic + model wrapper used to rank probes. - incident-bot/api/snooze_proxy.py: new POST /incidents/:id/snooze-scoped endpoint, authorizes against incident roles. - incident-bot/models/incident.py: add scoped_snoozes field and migration stub (safe default). - incident-bot/tests/unit/test_sculptor.py and tests/integration/test_snooze_flow.py - docs/triage-sculptor.md and console hint yml.

Testing & CI: initial CI run flagged a lint error and an intermittent integration timeout in the harness. Addressed linting (flake8 rule around mutable defaults) and added a retry/backoff to the harness; subsequent pipeline passed all unit/integration checks.

Observability: added metrics, traces, and an opt-in perf dashboard tile; will add alerting for queue depth > threshold during canary.

Review conversation (condensed): Kira Singh (reviewer) 2026-02-19: "Nice approach. Two asks: 1) make sure scoring config is dynamic via config service rather than hardcoded defaults, 2) can we add an acceptance test that simulates a severity escalation and ensures the snooze is revoked." Priya (author) 2026-02-20: "Thanks — updated scoring to pull from config service with sensible defaults and added the escalation acceptance test (tests/integration/test_snooze_escalation.py)." Luis Ortega (reviewer) 2026-02-21: "Worker uses Redis sorted set; we need to guard against unbounded memory if downstream consumers lag. Suggest TTL + periodic compaction." Priya 2026-02-22: "Added compaction task and per-entry TTL; documented limits. Also added metric triage.sculptor.stalled_compactions." Samir Patel (reviewer) 2026-02-22: "Minor: prefer 403 over 404 when authorization fails for snooze_proxy to avoid leaking existence info." Priya 2026-02-22: "Switched to 403 and added tests to assert behavior." Final reviewer state: approvals from Kira and Luis after changes, Samir approved after the auth change.

Merge notes: merged via squash on 2026-02-24 after green CI and approvals.

Post-merge runbook: - Enable triage_sculptor flag in staging for 48h observation - Enable snooze_proxy behind a Console beta with canary to a subset of SRE teams - Monitor triage.sculptor.queue_length and snooze.proxy.requests for anomalies - Rollback plan: disable flags + run compaction to clear queue if regressions observed

Known limitations and follow-ups: - Current scoring model is an experimental linear blend of heuristics; plan to train with historical incident outcome labels (ENG-8439). - Console UX for scoped snooze is minimal; backlog ticket created for richer interaction (ENG-8458). - Edge-case: cross-incident shared probes not fully deduplicated; follow-up optimization ticket created.

Overall impact: reduces noisy low-value probe runs during major incidents, gives on-call safe, scoped control to defer noisy checks, and provides observability to ensure the feature remains safe in production.
notes: Canary plan documented. No DB migration that requires downtime; migration adds nullable JSON column 'scoped_snoozes' to incidents. Migration is backward-compatible; code guards for older rows. Metrics and docs included.
